chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Ben Webster, the bad boy of Duke's band
summary: McRae tells how Webster stumbled into the pit at the Jump for Joy rehearsal and walked away from arguments at a Minton's gathering of tenor men.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Just couldn't be any musician to get into these bands. You had to carry yourself.

But this particular band -- Ben would always be there. He was the Peck's bad boy.

The band was opening the pit -- this big theater where they was opening this Jump For Joy Show -- where I took Ella to see the show. We had a front row seat. And the band was already in the pit. And Duke was just almost getting ready to come out, and the lights were going down. Here comes Ben. The band was sitting there quiet as a mouse. And everybody was just sitting. (inaudible), you know. And here comes Ben out stumbling, making noise, talking boo boo. That was Ben -- always Ben -- Ben was (inaudible) the same thing. One time we had a -- we all met at a summit -- musicians -- at 116th Street, The Minton Playhouse -- I think it was Dexter Gordon, four or five other top tenor players.
